author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected after the fact: the correction is offered with the visit's current date and description filled in, is judged on the same terms as a booking, and replaces that visit's details in place rather than leaving a second visit behind.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then the same form the booking uses is shown, carrying that visit's current date and description
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are submitted against it, then that visit's date and description are replaced and the owner's record is shown
given a booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet holds the same visits as before, one of them corrected, and no additional visit
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is shown again, and the description is named
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is shown again, and the date is named
given a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner, when a correction is attempted, then it is refused
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, still declined)
any link to the correction from the owner's record or any other page - the correction is reached directly in this slice
moving a visit to a different pet or owner
a page listing a pet's visits for selection
notes: NG-5 narrowed by owner decision 2026-08-28; recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-28-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md and in the PRD Non-Goals table. Reuse the existing visit form and its visit model attribute - the correction shows the same form as the booking. Two open questions are recorded in docs/prd.md and must not be resolved by implementation: where staff reach the correction from (no entry point ships here), and whether a visit whose date has already passed should be correctable in its description alone. Narrowest reading taken for the second: the booking date rule applies unchanged, so a past visit cannot keep its date through a correction (Visits edge case 4).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction is the forward-only edit pattern the codebase already demonstrates twice (owner details, pet details), applied to the third editable record. No new type, package, route family, dependency, or persistence path: the visit stays inside the Owner aggregate (system-design.md Contracts, 'Invariants the rows cannot carry'), and OwnerRepository.save remains the sole write path. The one adjustment is a parameter: VisitController's @ModelAttribute("visit") gains an optional visitId path variable and branches on it, exactly mirroring PetController.findPet's required=false petId (PetController.java:76). ADR 2026-08-28-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing already carries the product decision, so this slice needs no new ADR. system-design.md updated: VisitController, Owner, Pet, Visit and OwnerRepository rows now cite REQ-VIS-003, and the aggregate-invariant paragraph now records the identity-set property that makes an in-place correction possible.
integration_points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit join the existing VisitController; both are served by the same @ModelAttribute chain as the /visits/new pair
the corrected visit is written through OwnerRepository.save(owner) cascading over Pet.visits (cascade=ALL); no VisitRepository is introduced

the existing pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template serves both routes unchanged - it posts to the current URL (no action attribute) and keys its heading off visit['new'], which is false for a loaded visit

patterns.description: findPet: one @ModelAttribute serving both the create and the edit route via a required=false id path variable, returning a new instance when absent and the aggregate's existing instance when present. This is the shape loadPetWithVisit must take for visitId.

initUpdateForm/processUpdateForm: the edit route pair reuses the create route's view and validation, differing only in that it operates on a loaded entity. The correction route pair is structurally identical.

Owner.getPet(Integer): id-keyed lookup over the child collection. If the visit lookup is placed on the model rather than inline in the controller, Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirroring this is the precedent-following shape.

risks.risk: MECHANISM - duplicate visit row. loadPetWithVisit today unconditionally does 'Visit visit = new Visit(); pet.addVisit(visit); return visit;'. If the correction path reaches that code, the stray transient Visit stays in pet.visits, cascade-persists as a second row, and also trips @NotBlank on description at flush.
risks.mitigation: The correction path must construct nothing and call pet.addVisit nowhere. Branch loadPetWithVisit on a @PathVariable(name="visitId", required=false) Integer: null keeps today's booking behaviour verbatim; non-null locates the existing Visit inside pet.getVisits() by id and returns THAT instance. Spring MVC then binds the submitted date/description onto the instance already inside the aggregate (the handler's @Valid Visit parameter resolves to the same 'visit' model attribute), and it already carries its id, so owners.save(owner) cascades a MERGE and emits an UPDATE. Prefill (criterion 1) falls out for free, since th:object="${visit}" renders that loaded instance. Two properties make binding-in-place safe and were verified: BaseEntity declares no equals/hashCode, so the LinkedHashSet in Pet.visits is identity-keyed and mutating an element cannot rehash or duplicate it; and the existing setDisallowedFields("id","*.id") binder blocks id rebinding, so the identity comes only from the path. The defensive alternative - bind onto a fresh Visit, then copy date and description onto the located instance before save, as PetController.updatePetDetails does - is equivalent in effect and acceptable, but note updatePetDetails is copying an instance onto itself for the same reason, so the copy adds nothing here.

risks.risk: visitId is made a mandatory path variable on the shared @ModelAttribute, breaking the two /visits/new routes, which run the same method.
risks.mitigation: required=false, as PetController.findPet does for petId. Keep the null branch byte-identical to today's behaviour so REQ-VIS-001 and REQ-VIS-002 are untouched.

risks.risk: The 'no additional visit' criterion is asserted vacuously. VisitControllerTests stubs OwnerRepository with @MockitoBean, so save() is a no-op and a duplicate element would raise no persistence error - a test that only checks the redirect would pass against a broken implementation.
risks.mitigation: Assert on the aggregate, not on the response: the Owner the stub returns is the same instance the controller mutates, so after the POST assert pet.getVisits() has its original size, that the element with the target id carries the new date and description, and that no element is new (id == null). testing-principles.md tolerates extending the existing framework-stub fixture; the size-and-identity assertion is what gives the criterion teeth.

risks.risk: A visit whose date has already passed cannot be corrected at all, because the booking date rule rejects its unchanged date.
risks.mitigation: Deliberate - the PRD's narrowest reading, recorded as Visits edge case 4 and as an open question. Apply the future-date rule unchanged; do not soften it in implementation.

risks.risk: A new user-facing string for the correction (submit-button label or flash message) partly translates the UI and breaches REQ-LANG-002; I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails on a key missing from any of the eleven bundles.
risks.mitigation: No template change is needed for any acceptance criterion, so the cheapest correct answer is to ship none: the form already posts to the current URL and already drops the 'New' prefix for a loaded visit. If a distinct label is added anyway, the key goes into all eleven messages bundles in the same commit.

notes: Ownership refusal (criterion 6, Visits edge case 1) needs no new mechanism: with no VisitRepository, the only way to reach a visit is traversal from the owner in the path, so a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner, simply is not found. Refuse it the way loadPetWithVisit already refuses a bad ownerId or petId - IllegalArgumentException. That renders the error page, which is the existing convention for this controller; the PRD says only 'refused' and specifies no status. || Security: no new trust boundary. The route joins the existing set of unauthenticated mutating POSTs (system-design.md Threat Model, row 1) - that posture is the demonstration's and is out of scope here. The one slice-specific property is identifier tampering: the aggregate traversal above is the whole of the authorization available in this codebase, so resolve the visit by traversal and never by a global id lookup. The existing disallowed-fields binder covers the mass-assignment vector. || The prd-entry lists Owner.java and the visit template among file_targets. Neither is required by the recommended mechanism. Do not add an Owner.updateVisit(...) mutator to fill the list: that would move a business rule into the model while system-design.md Open Question 2 (business rules in controllers, no service layer) is unsettled, and the sibling booking rule sits in the controller today. Consistency with the unsettled status quo is correct here; that question gets settled project-wide or not at all. A pure id-keyed lookup on Pet, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer), is fine if the implementer wants the traversal off the controller. || No design-doc-autofix records in the log - autofix audit skipped. || Vocabulary: ubiquitous-language.md lists Booking and Amendment on Visit's Avoid line; 'correct a booked visit' uses 'booked' as a participle, not as a name for the record, so no drift. Prose term stays 'Visit'.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: No test in the suite verifies that processUpdateVisitForm actually calls owners.save(owner). theVisitCorrectionShouldReplaceTheBookedVisitDetails and theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddAnotherVisitToThePet assert on pet.getVisits() after the POST, but that mutation happens purely through Spring MVC's data binding onto the aggregate's own Visit instance (loadPetWithVisit returns pet.getVisit(visitId) directly) - a state change that occurs whether or not this.owners.save(owner) is ever reached. Deleting the save() call from processUpdateVisitForm would not fail either test. The design-block at handoff.jsonl line 8 states 'the save call is covered by VisitControllerTests asserting on the aggregate,' but that claim conflates in-memory mutation-via-binding with the actual repository write - the two are independent in this mocked slice (OwnerRepository.save is a MockitoBean no-op). The @Transactional integration test cannot close this gap either, by the design-block's own admission (risk 2 at line 8): keeping the entity managed for the whole test lets Hibernate dirty-checking persist the correction regardless of whether save() runs. Net effect: no test in the suite currently proves the save() call in processUpdateVisitForm is exercised or necessary, even though system-design.md records open-in-view=false as the property that makes the write path load-bearing in production.
findings.fix: Add Mockito.verify(this.owners).save(owner) (or same(owner)) to theVisitCorrectionShouldReplaceTheBookedVisitDetails, following the existing verify(...) pattern already used in OwnerControllerTests.java:171/183.

findings.description: prd.md REQ-VIS-003 'Done when' criterion 6 and Visits edge case 3 both name two refusal scenarios: 'a visit that does not belong to the named pet, OR a pet that does not belong to the named owner.' theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitDoesNotBelongToThePet covers only the first half (a visitId absent from the pet's own visit set). No test exercises a correction attempted against a pet that does not belong to the named owner, on either the booking or the correction route. Since loadPetWithVisit's owner-then-pet traversal is the sole authorization mechanism for this controller (per the design-block's security note at handoff.jsonl line 8), this half of the documented acceptance criterion is currently unverified.
findings.fix: Add a case (e.g. theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenThePetDoesNotBelongToTheOwner) posting to the correction route with a petId that exists but is not one of the stubbed owner's pets, asserting the same IllegalArgumentException root cause.

approved_aspects: theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddAnotherVisitToThePet and theVisitCorrectionShouldReplaceTheBookedVisitDetails assert on pet.getVisits() directly rather than on the redirect, which does give the 'no additional visit' criterion teeth in the @WebMvcTest slice: the stubbed OwnerRepository still returns the real, mutable Owner/Pet graph the controller operates on, so a regression to the unconditional 'new Visit(); pet.addVisit(visit);' branch in loadPetWithVisit would leave a second element in pet.getVisits() (hasSize(1) fails) with isNew()==true (allMatch fails), and would also break theVisitCorrectionShouldReplaceTheBookedVisitDetails's singleElement assertion - consistent with the implementer's mutation-check claim at handoff.jsonl line 6, which static analysis of loadPetWithVisit and Pet.getVisit(Integer) corroborates.

The split between the extended @WebMvcTest slice (VisitControllerTests) and the new @SpringBootTest+real-H2 integration test (VisitControllerIntegrationTests) is the right call under testing-principles.md's Mocking Policy: the new integration test reaches for real I/O first for the one property a mocked repository cannot observe (cascade persistence adding a genuine second row), while the slice test extends the pre-existing framework-stub fixture rather than introducing a new mock, which the brief explicitly tolerates.

New/modified tests follow the BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming school, use chained AssertJ assertions (extracting/containsExactly, singleElement) with no JUnit assertEquals/assertTrue, avoid phase-comment narration, and use role-named Tier-1 constants (BOOKED_VISIT_DATE, CORRECTED_VISIT_DESCRIPTION, VISIT_ID_OF_ANOTHER_PET) with no mystery literals.

Validation-refusal criteria (blank description, non-future date) and the prefill criterion are each covered by a dedicated, single-concern test with view/status/field-error assertions matching the PRD's 'Done when' wording.
./gradlew test on both files passes cleanly against the real Gradle build (H2, Hibernate, MockMvc all exercised without failures).

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Non-blocking hardening. processUpdateVisitForm declares @ModelAttribute Owner owner, so the new correction POST binds request parameters onto the loaded Owner aggregate and then persists it via owners.save(owner). A request to /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit carrying address, city, telephone, firstName, lastName, or an indexed nested path such as pets[0].name writes those values to the owner record, even though the correction form offers none of them; the Owner itself is not @Valid on this path, so only the JPA pre-update bean-validation pass constrains the values. This does not leave the application weaker than the baseline in docs/system-design.md#security-context: the identical binding exists on the sibling processNewVisitForm and on PetController.processCreationForm/processUpdateForm, and /owners/{ownerId}/edit already accepts the same writes from any unauthenticated caller, so the new route adds no capability an attacker lacks. It is recorded because the new endpoint replicates the pattern and the remedy is one keyword and behavior-preserving (the Owner is needed only as the save target; the corrected Visit is already the instance inside the aggregate). Class sweep for request-bound aggregate roots across src/main/java/.../owner: the three sibling handlers named above are the only other instances, and all are outside this change set.
findings.fix: Change the parameter to @ModelAttribute(binding = false) Owner owner in processUpdateVisitForm so the aggregate root is resolved from the model but never bound from the request. Optionally apply the same to processNewVisitForm as a follow-up outside this slice.

approved_aspects: IDOR refused by construction: loadPetWithVisit resolves owner from the path via owners.findById, then owner.getPet(petId), then the new Pet.getVisit(visitId), which scans only that pet's own visits set. A visitId belonging to another pet or another owner returns null and the handler throws before any handler body runs, so no cross-aggregate visit is reachable. Pet.getVisit additionally skips unsaved visits (!visit.isNew()) and compares ids with Objects.equals, so a null or unmatched id cannot fall through to a wrong element.

Error path leaks nothing: the IllegalArgumentException messages carry only the caller's own path integers (a non-numeric visitId fails @PathVariable Integer conversion with a 400 before the method runs). templates/error.html renders ${message} through th:text, which Thymeleaf escapes, so no reflected XSS and no internal detail beyond the pre-existing owner/pet message pattern.

Mass assignment on identifiers is genuinely blocked on the new handlers: the @InitBinder setDisallowedFields(id, *.id) is controller-scoped, so it applies to every WebDataBinder in VisitController including the ones for the new GET and POST edit handlers, for both the visit and the owner model attributes. Visit carries only date and description beyond the inherited id, so a correction cannot rebind the visit's identity or move it to another pet; the template's hidden petId field binds to nothing on Visit.

Bind-in-place on a rejected correction cannot persist. spring.jpa.open-in-view=false (src/main/resources/application.properties:11) ends the persistence context with the owners.findById call, so the returned graph is detached when binding mutates it. The rejection path returns the view name and calls no transactional method, so no flush occurs; the pet's visits are EAGER-fetched, so template rendering triggers no lazy initialization and hence no new transaction. Verified against the code, not taken from the design note.

Output escaping intact: templates/pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders every request-derived value (pet name, visit description, owner name, previous visits) through th:text with no th:utext, inline JavaScript, or unescaped fragment, and the change disables no escaping.

No new attack surface beyond the two declared routes, and both are documented as to what they expose (docs/system-design.md Contracts row for VisitController names the traversal-based resolution; docs/prd.md REQ-VIS-003 states no page links to the correction). No new dependency, no build.gradle change, so the supply-chain surface is unchanged; no repository or actuator exposure widened; no credential, token, or key-shaped literal anywhere in the diff.
Data access remains parameterized: the change adds no query, only in-memory traversal over the already-loaded aggregate through OwnerRepository derived queries.

author: change-grader
summary: add in-place correction route for a booked visit

blast_radius.note: Nine files, but only two production files in one package: Pet gains a pure id-keyed getVisit lookup, VisitController gains one route pair and an extracted date helper, and the shared model-attribute loader's null-visitId branch is byte-identical to the prior booking behaviour, so REQ-VIS-001 and REQ-VIS-002 are untouched; the other five files are PRD, ADR and system-design prose, and no sensitive path is touched.

semantic_surprise.note: processUpdateVisitForm declares a request-bound Owner parameter and then calls owners.save(owner), so the new correction POST binds and persists arbitrary Owner fields - firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone, or a nested pets[0].name - even though the form offers only date and description; the InitBinder disallows ids alone, so a route whose stated job is correcting two visit fields is in fact a new unauthenticated write surface on the owner aggregate.

test_adequacy.note: The tests exercise the changed behaviour rather than restating it: six unit tests cover prefill, in-place replacement with a verify on save of the same owner instance, no-extra-visit, both refusal rules and both traversal refusals, and a new SpringBootTest integration test drives the real repository and re-reads from the database, which is the only place a duplicate visit row is observable; the one uncovered path is that a refused correction must not persist the values binding already wrote onto the aggregate's Visit, a risk the design record closes by spring.jpa.open-in-view=false and no test pins.

reviewer_hedging.note: Three of the four dispatched reviewers approve with empty findings, but security-reviewer's approval carries an open autofix finding tagged with the secure-by-design bar clause, carried forward unchanged from pass 1 and deliberately left unremediated on baseline-parity grounds, with its one-keyword fix named and declined; doc-reviewer also records an out-of-slice CLAUDE.md Gradle-task mismatch.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries and zero consultations; the single design revision was a re-triage that widened the design record to cover three ADR and README doc paths after an autofix-audit mismatch, not a scope fight, and the diff matches the superseding record's paths, ships no entry-point link as the PRD demands, and leaves cancellation and deletion declined.

rationale: Correct, well-tested and tightly scoped, but the new correction POST binds and saves the whole Owner aggregate, so a date-and-description-only route accepts owner-field writes in fact. Read VisitController's update handler and decide whether to take the declined non-binding fix before merging.
